RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday,  the November 25, 2005/Agrahayana 4, 1927 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs, Food
and Public Distribution; Environment and Forests; Food Processing Industries;
Health and Family Welfare; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions — 20
Environmental clearance to Balachaur-
Hoshiarpur-Dasuya highway
*41. SHRI VARINDER SINGH
BAJWA : Will the Minister of
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether a proposal sent by the
Punjab Government for removing/cutting
of trees for upgradation of the Balachaur-
Hoshiarpur-Dasuya highway is pending for
environmental clearance;
(b) if so, since when the request is
pending; and
(c) by when, the clearance is likely to
be accorded?
Commissions/Committees on rail
accidents
*42. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:  Will
the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to
state :
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
has decided to set up a special commission/
committee to find out the reasons/causes
of rail accidents;
(b) if so, the total number of such
Commissions/Committees set up by
Government during the last three months,
month-wise; and
(c) when the reports of the
Commissions/Committees are expected to
be received by Government?
Relaxation of  Coastal Zonal
Regulation
*43. SHRI PRAMOD MAHAJAN :
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state :
(a) whether the State Government of
Maharashtra has sought the relaxation of
Coastal Zonal Regulation, 1991 for some
areas in Mumbai;
(b) if so, the names of such areas;
(c) the reaction of the Central
Government thereto; and
(d) the reasons for not accepting the
proposal?
Encouraging investment in agricultural
marketing infrastructure projects
*44. SHRI MOOLCHAND MEENA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of  AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided

14
to come out with an innovative scheme to
encourage entrepreneurs investing in
agricultural marketing infrastructure
projects;
(b) if so, whether this move is aimed at
bringing down risk threat for both
entrepreneurs and banks;
(c) whether venture capital scheme was
part of Government's effort to bridge the
gap between producer and consumer;
(d) whether the scheme covers a wide
range of agricultural and allied sectors'
activities including collection, cleaning,
grading, quality certification, labelling,
packing, ripening chambers, retailing,
wholesale and value addition facilities; and
(e) if so, by when these schemes are
likely to be implemented?
Revival of IISCO
*45.  SHRI  KALRAJ  MISHRA:  Will
the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Indian Iron and Steel
Company continues to be a loss-making
concern, if so, the production, profit and
loss incurred by each of its units since 2001
onwards;
(b) whether some of its units have been
lying idle fully or partially, if so, the details
thereof; and
(c) the steps taken and proposed to be
taken to revive the same and the strategy
contemplated to revive and rejuvenate this
PSU?
National Accreditation Board
*46. SHRI JESUDASU SEELAM:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to  state :
(a) whether Government have
announced formation of a task force
comprising experts from the Ministries of
Health and Family Welfare, Tourism,
Railways, External Affairs, Civil Aviation
and Director General of Health Services to
suggest strengthening the policy measures
and norms for National Accreditation
Board to provide accreditation to private
hospitals;
(b) whether Government will also come
out with Clinical Establishment Act;
(c) whether Government have also
announced that policy decision for granting
of medical visa will also be considered; and
(d) whether the Ministry of Tourism
will also aid the Ministry in giving strategic
push to Indian health-care sector in foreign
markets?
Passenger-upgrade scheme
*47. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA : Will
the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to
 state :
(a) whether the free passenger-upgrade
scheme announced recently by Railways
is operational;
(b) if so, the total amount saved, so far,
by Railways on account of not having to
refund money for waitlisted tickets;
(c) if not, by when the scheme would
be made operational; and
(d) the launch status of other passenger-
friendly services by Railways, like bundling
of hotel services alongwith train ticket
bookings?
Dioxins in eggs
*48.  SHRI THENNALA G.
BALAKRISHNA PILLAI:
 DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state :
(a) whether it is a fact that an NGO

15
called "Toxic Link" has reported that eggs
produced in the country contain high level
of dioxins which is a poisonous chemical;
(b) if so, the facts of the matter; and
(c) the corrective measures taken by the
Government in this regard?
Shortage of onion
†*49. DR. PRABHA THAKUR :
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI :
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state :
(a) whether it is a fact that there was
acute shortage of onion in the month of
October in the country which necessitated
import of onion;
(b) the names of the countries
wherefrom Government imported onion
alongwith the value of onion imported,
country-wise; and
(c) the reasons for the shortage of onion
and the reasons for not overcoming the
situation in time?
Pulse production
*50. SHRI R. K. ANAND : Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state :
(a) whether it is a fact that the Green
Revolution which made India self-sufficient
in wheat and rice had ignored pulses; and
(b) whether it is also a fact that India
imported pulses to the tune of 1701.16
thousand tonnes worth Rs. 2251.20 crores
in 2003-04?
Cutting down the production cost by
SAIL
†*51. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
 Will the Minister of  STEEL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Steel
Authority of India has decided to
implement a scheme by spending Rs. 400
crores in order to cut down the production
cost;
(b) if so, the details of the said scheme;
(c) the percentage of reduction in the
existing steel production cost expected after
the completion of this scheme; and
(d) the profit of the organisation in terms
of amount expected as a result of reduction
in the production cost?
Popularising SDF in sugar industry
*52. SHRIMATI JAMANA DEVI
BARUPAL:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
 Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION  be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is poor response from
sugar industry to Sugar Development Fund
for modernization or expansion of plants;
(b) if so, the main reasons for the same;
(c) whether Government have urged
sugar industry to improve quality of sugar
to make it internationally acceptable;
(d) whether Government are ready to
ease the conditions so that more and more
industrialists are interested in utilizing this
fund; and
(e) the total amount, so far, provided to
sugar industry from this fund?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

16
Bird Flu
*53. SHRI PYARELAL KHANDELWAL:
SHRI UDAY PRATAP SINGH:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that World Health
Organisation has warned of spreading of
Bird Flu in India;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have taken
measures to check spreading of Bird Flu in
the country; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Cases in District Consumer Courts
*54. DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA: Will the Minister of
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to
state:
(a) the total number of new cases
registered in various District Consumer
Courts during 2004 in the country;
(b) the total number of old cases
pending disposal as on 1st January, 2004;
(c) out of total cases, how many were
disposed of during 2004 and whether the
disposal was more than new registrations;
(d) whether inordinate delay is being
caused in the disposal of consumer cases;
and
(e) if so, the remedial measures intended
to be taken?
Task Force on drug price control
*55. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
 Will the Minister of CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether present price control policy
for drugs is blocking entry of new drugs
and the PMs Task Force on drugs has
recommended fixing a ceiling on prices,
which could be flexible and linked to
wholesale price index;
(b) whether this Task Force headed by
Shri Pranob Sen was set up to look into
ways to make drugs available at reasonable
prices;
(c) whether it has already submitted its
recommendations to his Ministry;
(d) if so, the details thereof and how
many of the recommendations have been
accepted; and
(e) the steps being taken to implement
them?
Losses of Railways
*56. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
SHRI RAASHID ALVI:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Railways
have lost nearly Rs. 2000 crores over the
delay in using recycled scrap to
manufacture wheels;
(b) whether during 2004-05 Budget it
had been promised that 1 million tonnes of
scrap that is generated each year would no
longer be sold but would be recycled to
make wheels in the factory;
(c) whether due to non-implementation
of this decision Railways have incurred a
loss of Rs. 2000 crore; and
(d) if so, the main reasons for delay and
by what time a final decision in this regard
is likely to be taken?

17
Research on elimination of pesticides
*57. SHRIMATI MOHSINA KIDWAI:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
farmers in Penta Srirampuram in Andhra
Pradesh have managed to eliminate
pesticides from their rice crop by following
a three-step procedure as evolved by their
agricultural officer;
(b) if so, whether this innovative
method will be studied by the agricultural
scientists of ICAR with a view to ensuring
its application on a selective basis
depending upon soil; and
(c) if so, by when?
Shortage of onion/wheat production
*58. SHRI DARA SINGH: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the production of onion/
wheat in the country is expected to be less
than the target during 2005-06;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons for this shortfall;
(c) whether Government propose to
import onion/wheat this year in order to
meet the shortage; and
(d) if so, the details thereof country-
wise and quantity-wise and the total
expenditure likely to be involved therein
during the current year?
Ongoing railway projects in Southern
Railways
*59. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA:
 Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of the ongoing Railway
projects under the Southern Railways;
(b) the details of the estimated costs
alongwith details of funds allocated to each
of these projects, project-wise;
(c) whether it is a fact that most of the
project works are not progressing
satisfactorily due to inadequate fund
allotments;
(d) if so, whether steps have been taken
to release adequate funds to speed up the
completion of these works;
(e) if  so, details thereof, project-wise;
and
(f) if not, the reason therefor?
Rail infrastructure in Orissa
*60. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B. J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of  RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
industrialization of Orissa would
necessitate development of rail
infrastructure particularly from Jaipur,
Paradip, Gopalpur, Jharsuguda, Raigada,
etc.;
(b) whether this will also necessitate
immediate rail linkage from Kalahandi to
Gopalpur to meet the needs of
industrialization of the backward areas with
a view to improving the economy of this
region; and
(c) if so, the action plan of Government
to address this issue?
NEW DELHI; YOGENDRA NARAIN,

Identification of new varieties of
wheat by ICAR
292. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be

(a) whether it is a fact that the ICAR
has identified seven new varieties of wheat
for release;

conditions in the country; and

to get from these new varieties?

†293. SHRIMATI KAMLA

removed; and

previously set in the macro-management
scheme?

Punjab and other parts of the country; and

measures including legal support

magur?

rain in Vidarbha region of Maharashtra in
October, 2005;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have sent a
Central team there to assess the damage

of reorganization of the system;

based at Bhubaneswar in Orissa and what
is the action plan of Government to adjust
its staff, once it is closed down;

SHRIMATI PREMA

be pleased to state:
(a) the total consumption of pesticides
in the country and the total number of
pesticide producing companies in the
country;

companies are providing sub-standard
pesticides to the farmers as a result of which

RAO: Will the Minister of

going to release some of the new varieties

(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) how those new varieties are different
from the existing ones?

the Minister of AGRICULTURE be

floods and droughts that hit different parts

(b) the amount of financial aid provided

expenditure of money provided to States

Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
